# All People’s Park

- Source URL: https://townofglover.com/all-peoples-park/
- Final URL: https://townofglover.com/all-peoples-park/
- Crawled: 2026-07-30T19:05:06.964704+00:00
- Page type: page
- Published/updated: 2024-08-29T12:25:09+00:00 2024-08-29T12:26:23+00:00

## Page content

Glover Park is located at Line Drive off Vt Route 122 and near Vt Rt 16.

It offers to the public:

a youth baseball field with timber frame dugouts

an adult softball field with timber frame dugouts and the grey monster

batting cage

pump track

Timber frame community pavilion with mural and climbing wall.

Timber frame covered bridge play structure

All persons inclusive forest and field sensory trail

Universal design natural play areas

Picnic area with cedar benches

Garden beds

Coming in 2025 Pickleball

# GLOVER NEIGHBORS – phone tree project

- Source URL: https://townofglover.com/glover-neighbors-phone-tree-project/
- Final URL: https://townofglover.com/glover-neighbors-phone-tree-project/
- Crawled: 2026-07-30T19:06:40.597719+00:00
- Page type: page
- Published/updated: 2020-04-14T12:52:23+00:00 2020-04-15T14:49:41+00:00

## Page content

In response to the COVID-19 pandemic Glover Ambulance and a group of Glover residents have started organizing a phone tree that could be used to spread relevant information throughout the town or to gather information from town residents. This phone tree could be a useful tool as the present situation develops or in the event of an extended power outage or natural disaster.

Our plan is to divide the town into 4 quarters with a town wide coordinator (Bethany Dunbar 525-3545) and coordinators for each quarter (Northwest – Ann Creaven, – 673-0515; Northeast – Tabitha Armstrong – 323-6966 & Lila Winstead – 525-1017; Southwest – Barb Delzio – 236-2115; Southeast – Mariel Hess – 525-6638 & Sara Gluckman 525-3188). The divisions can be seen on the town 911 map. Click on the map link below.

The coordinators will work to find volunteers who know their neighborhoods or sections of their roads and are willing to help collect contact information and to make calls as the need arises. Ideally, no one person would have more than 10 calls to make, and one or more of those contacts would then call their list of 10 further contacts.

We know that Glover residents already look out for each other through many family, neighbor-to-neighbor, and church based connections. We are not trying to compete with these existing networks, but to connect with them and to work to find those residents who are not covered and would like to be.

If you would like to be part of this project, or to know more about it, answer the questions in the survey or call one of the section coordinators. Coordinator’s contact info is listed above and on the map.

MAP LINK: Phone Tree Map

## Page content

### Glover Town Clerks Office

phone (802) 525-6227 fax (802) 525-4115 HOURS: 7:00 am- 5:00 pm Monday – Thursday Closed Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays, and Holidays Cindy Epinette, Clerk/Treasurer Email

Town Clerk’s Office Services

Zoning: There is no zoning in Glover. If you are building or remodeling around the lakes, you need to contact ANR to learn about their requirements.

Driveway permit is required. Applications are available at the town clerk’s office.

Vault time, $4.00 per hour for research, there is a charge for copies, we do not fax and we do not do title searches.

Motor Vehicle registration renewal for the current month and two months prior, must be check or money order payable to Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) for the amount due, $3.00 charge for the town cash or check.

Select Board Meetings the 2nd and 4th Thursday of the month at 6:30 PM at the Town Hall. To get on the agenda call the Town Clerk’s Office, All meetings are open to the public.

Dog licenses due April 1st, bring certificates for spayed females and neutered males and rabies vaccination.

Prices: Male & Female $15.00 Spayed/Neutered $ 11.00 After April First: Male & Female $19.00 Spayed/Neutered $ 13.00

Town of Glover Dog and Wolf-hybrid ordinance

Glover Cemeteries French Cemetery -full Andersonville Cemetery – full West Glover Cemetery – full Westlook Cemetery – lots available on right side of cemetery next to Route 122 Westlook II Cemetery

Hours:Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday 1-6 p.m.;Saturday, 10:00 – 12:00 (Winter only)PlayWorld – Tuesday 9:00 – 11:00 (during school year)Call for summer event schedules.For more information, call Toni Eubanks at 525-4365.

#### Roads

Town Garage 802-525-4025

#### Rubbish Removal

Bagged household trash can be brought to Glover Recycling. Charges per bag are:$3 – Kitchen size bag$5 – 30 gallon size bag$8 – Contractor size bag

Our dumpster is limited in size, so PLEASE, if you are cleaning out and have a pickup load of trash take it directly to the landfill in Coventry.

Residents should make their own arrangements with private haulers, or they may take their garbage to Waste U.S.A. in Coventry.Following is a list of private garbage haulers operating in Glover.

Chayer’s Rubbish Removal – 802 673-3376Call for rates. Dave’s Rubbish – 802-334-5757Residential and commercial. Weekly and bi-weekly pickups available, call for rates. Available are Roll-offs, dumpsters, and 96-gallon carts for residential service.

Myers – 800-981-5213 and Local Number 802-748-3973. Call for residential and commercial rates.

Casella Waste Management – 800-639-3083 or direct line at 888 485-1469Rate depends on frequency and volume. Recyclable materials can be picked up.

ALL Metals – 802 472-5100 Scrap metal and construction debris and roll offs.

# Heart of Glover

- Source URL: https://townofglover.com/heart-of-glover/
- Final URL: https://townofglover.com/heart-of-glover/
- Crawled: 2026-07-30T19:07:43.565079+00:00
- Page type: page
- Published/updated: 2021-06-28T12:29:29+00:00 2026-05-04T11:48:21+00:00

## Page content

What is the Village Plan?

This plan represents an opportunity to develop a shared vision for the Glover Village. By working to engage the community throughout the summer of 2021, this plan is intended to develop a community driven design for a Town Green and streetscape that will invite residents, travellers, and businesses to linger in the beautiful and unique Village of Glover, Vermont.

Schedule

These dates will be updated as the Glover Planning Commission proceeds:

- July / August – Community Tabling Events and Public Survey at Glover Farmers Market and Recycling Center
- September – Community Visioning Meeting and Public Survey Results held virtually on Zoom
- Early Winter 2021 – Heart of Glover Village Plan Presentation & Public Critique
- 2022 – Heart of Glover Village Plan Presented to Selectboard
Community Visioning MeetingThe Glover Planning Commission and our consultant Dubois & King held a virtual town meeting on September 20 to review preliminary design concepts for the village green and Rt 16 corridor through Glover center. You can review the presentations and conversations that we had at this meeting by reading the meeting notes. We invite you to review these designs and provide us with feedback on them. We have provided a “scorecard” for you to provide this feedback.

The concepts can be viewed here: tinyurl.com/GloverPosters

You can complete the scorecard here: tinyurl.com/GloverConceptSurvey

For a further explanation of the elements in the designs as well as a printable “scorecard”, please go here: tinyurl.com/GloverExplanation

We will be soliciting community input into these designs until October 20, 2021 at which point the consultants will be developing final proposed designs for the village green and Rt 16 corridor. We will plan to meet again as a community later this winter to review these designs. Stay tuned. . .

Who is leading this effort?

The Heart of Glover – Village Plan is being led by the Glover Planning Commission and supported by planning consultants from Dubois & King. If you have questions or concerns about the project, don’t hesitate to reach out via email to glovertc@comcast.net or call 525-6227.

Updates

As this project progresses, this website will be updated with meeting records, plan documents, and other related information as they become available.

## Page content

Shadow Lake Association

Lake Parker Association

Proposed Spillway Downstream Hazard EvaluationShadow Lake Dam, Glover, Vermont

FROM: Andrew Sampsell, P.E. – Dam Safety Program (DSP) – Dam Safety Engineer Benjamin Green, P.E. – DSP – Dam Safety Engineer, Steven Hanna – DSP – Dam Safety Engineer

TO: Town of Glover – Dam Owner

Hydrologic and Hydraulic Assessment for Shadow Lake Dam Alternatives. Weston & Sampson sent this to the Vermont Dam Safety Engineer Program. VTDEC DSP is reviewing the hydraulic models for various rehabilitation alternatives.

We don’t have a timeline for how long that will take.

HEC-RAS : Hydraulic Engineering Center River Analysis Software

HEC – HMS Crucial tool used for dam management and flood control.

Powerful tool used for dam safety risk.

Regional Priority Projects are high priority economic and community development projects that meet certain eligibility requirements (see priority project form). The Regional Project Prioritization (RPP) lists are used by federal, state, regional and local organizations to understand the funding needs of the region and allow regional economic and community development staff to help match federal and state funding announcements to projects. The Regional Project Prioritization (RPP) lists express the highest priority projects for each region and the top ten projects from each county will be included in a consolidated statewide list, which is submitted bi-annually to the Vermont Agency of Commerce and Community Development (ACCD), to be used by state and federal agencies when making funding decisions. Lists are developed and review annually. Attached is Glover’s Regional Project Prioritization (RPP) application. We will inform the town once it is accepted.

Support letters for Glover’s request to the Northeastern Vermont Development Association, for inclusion in the Regional Project Prioritization, will facilitate efforts to secure funding for repairs on the Shadow Lake Dam.

### Weston & Sampson drilled borings at Shadow Lake Dam on Thursday, June 5th.

Weston & Sampson Phone Conversation August 7, 2025 In Thomas’s voice.

7/24/2025 Weston & Sampson Update:

- Working on setting up a meeting with Ben Green to discuss the possibility of extending the dam on the left and right sides on to private properties that would be purchased by the town to allow raising of the dam crest and maintaining historic lake levels.
- Stability analysis nearly complete. It appears the downstream slope of the dam meets the minimum factor of safety requirements provided the dam maintains 1.5 feet of freeboard during the design storm.
- The seepage analysis indicates an inadequate factor of safety values, which should not be a surprise since seepage through the dam is observed. Seepage through the dam when water levels rise above historic lake levels is a deficiency that will need to be addressed. We will likely control seepage with the use of sand filters installed within the dam embankment.
- The poor condition of the auxiliary spillway and persistent seepage below this spillway is another deficiency that will need to be addressed. We are currently looking at the most cost-effective measures to correct this deficiency.
- We (Weston & Sampson and the town) should meet at some point in August to discuss the dam rehabilitation alternative the town would like to pursue. I assume that this will be largely dependent on the town purchasing private properties on both sides of the dam and the opinion of VT DSP to allow raising of the dam crest. We need the selected alternative to run our model and review results with VT DSP.
Update: July 22, 2025 Shadow Lake Boat Launch

Two Signs have been erected at the Boat Launch.

The sand that has gathered at the bottom of the cement launch pad has been considered and hopefully will be removed by Fish and Wildlife.

They measured the depth of the water, took photos, and located the end of the boat launch.

I will continue to keep you updated regarding new information.

Theresa

As you all know the boat launch is problematic with the lowering of the lake. I contacted Mike Wichrowski with Fish and Wildlife to discuss the boat ramp because they are the party responsible.

He appreciates that I informed them of the situation, although he had already heard about our situation through Ben Green, VT Dam Safety Engineer. Fish and Wildlife will be involved from this point forward to deal with the launch reconstruction. I let him know that it is likely the lake will stay at the 2′ lower level.

They are extremely busy this year and will begin the process of investigating the launch and survey data to gather information on the existing launch. It is possible that it is the only thing they will accomplish this year.

He will put the launch on his list of things to do and begin the process of renovating the launch. That includes surveys, elevation study, permits, dredging, etc. He is also going to include the problematic situation with the boat wash runoff. He was already aware of that problem and plans to include it in the engineering and design of the reconstruction of the launch.

Apparently, had I told him in January of the situation he may have been able to solve this problem this year. However, I told him I only found out about the “Permanent” drop of 2′ just this past month when we received the scenarios of the dam.

I am pleased with the nugget of hope in the remedy of the boat launch.

Theresa Perron

Spillway Modification Alternatives

Audio

Update: 4/22/25

Weston and Sampson engineers have evaluated several alternatives to correct deficiencies at the dam and plan to discuss advantages and disadvantages of each alternative with the town over the next few weeks.

Update: 4/1/2025

Weston & Sampson Engineers finished up incorporating the new survey data into hydraulic models (HEC-HMS) provided by DSP. This updated model allows us to evaluate spillway modification alternatives so the dam can pass the design storm. This evaluation should be completed towards the end of this week. Once these alternatives are developed, we will run them through additional hydraulic models (HEC-RAS) to assess downstream impacts, which is a critical aspect of this project. In the next week or so, we should be in a position to review alternatives with you.

More info here: https://shadowlakedam.org/

# Recycling Center

- Source URL: https://townofglover.com/recycling-center/
- Final URL: https://townofglover.com/recycling-center/
- Crawled: 2026-07-30T19:08:28.681785+00:00

- Published/updated: 2023-01-06T14:07:26+00:00 2026-07-09T11:28:34+00:00

## Page content

A to Z Guide to recycling: https://www.nekwmd.org/a-z-disposal-guide

Info: What can be Recycled.

These materials can be recycled in Glover. They must be sorted into the groups listed here. Please sort materials at home to save time and space at the Recycling Center.All materials must be reasonably clean – not washed with soap, but rinsed clean.

Winter Hours: December 1st through March 31st – Saturdays 9:00 to noon only

Summer Hours: April 1st through November 30th – Wednesdays 12 Noon to 3 PM/ Saturdays 9:00 to noon

NEWSPAPERS, MAGAZINES, OFFICE PAPER, JUNK MAIL: Can be mixed together – Includes catalogs, telephone books, glossy inserts and paperback books as well as colored paper, white paper, wrapping paper and junk mail. Any color or type of paper can be in this category except brown Kraft paper bags and boxboard (see next category), no paper with metal foil.

CORRUGATED CARDBOARD & BROWN KRAFT PAPER BAGS & BOXBOARD: NO wax-coated cardboard or cardboard soiled with food (pizza boxes, for example). Remove excess tape. Staples and some tape are OK. Please Flatten Boxes – no strings, plastic handles, or bags with plastic layers.

TIN CANS: Labels are OK. Flattening not required, please rinse. Separate from aluminum cans (A magnet will stick to tin but not to aluminum). Please Rinse Clean

ALUMINUM CANS, FOIL AND FOOD TRAYS: Labels OK. Please Rinse Clean

GLASS (ALL COLORS): BOTTLES & JARS ONLY – Clear, green, blue, and amber bottles and jars. Please rinse. NO crystal, no lids (plastic, metal or wood). NO light bulbs. All fluorescent bulbs are recyclable in a separate category.

#1, #2, #3, #4 & some #5 plastic containers: 2 gallon size maximum. Look for the recycling number and triangle stamped on the container. PLEASE RINSE CLEAN. #5 FOOD AND DRINK CONTAINERS ONLY. Labels are OK. NO automotive product containers are acceptable (motor oil, antifreeze, etc). No vinyl siding, NO STYROFOAM (even if it has a number).

PLASTIC BAGS: Plastic bags will no longer be accepted. There is no market for them. Some bags can be returned to Price Chopper.

ELECTRONICS: Computers, Televisions, Radios, Cable converter boxes, Scanners, DVD players, Answering machines, Fax machines, VCRs, Video game systems, Cordless phones, Stereo components

(receiver, tape deck, amplifier, CD player, equalizers).

FOOD SCRAPS: We accept all types of food scraps. No compostable plastic bags. Coffee filters and tea bags (with plastic tags removed) are the only acceptable paper. More information on the back of this Page.

Styrofoam- We accept foam coolers, foam packaging, egg cartons, meat trays; we do not accept flexible foam, packaging, packing peanuts, pipe insulation, insulation board.

Revised 1/2023

GLOVER ALSO ACCEPTS:

Aerosol cans, Fluorescent Bulbs of all types, Hard covered Books, Lead fishing sinkers, Mercury Containing Devices (thermostats, thermometers, etc), Used Motor Oil, Oil Filters, Batteries of all kinds, & Scrap Metal, including appliances (stoves, wash machines), but not including refrigerators, freezers, dehumidifiers, or air conditioners which can be taken to the Waste District facility in Lyndonville so refrigerants can be drained properly.

Glover is a member of the Northeast Kingdom Waste Management District

TIRES:

MUST BRING THEM TO Northeast Kingdom Waste Management District

224 Church Street, Lyndonville, VT 05851 and you must call first: Tel: 802.626.3532

- Tires 20” or less without rim $5.00/each
- Tires 20” or less with rim $10.00/each
- Tires 20.5” to 24.5” without rim $15.00/each
- Tires 20.5” to 24.5” with rim $30.00/each
CLOTHING AND TEXTILES – Drop and Swaps are held in the spring and fall in Derby.HOUSHOLD HAZARDOUS WASTE – BY APPOINTMENT ONLY, Monday -Friday, June through the end of September in Lyndonville, and special events throughout the District, June through September. Fees apply for business wastes. Call for details: 802 626-3532

Lyndonville Recycling is open to residents of all NEKWMD Towns 224 Church StreetWednesday 8am – 4pm & Saturday 8am – 3pmOn the web at www.nekwmd.org, e-mail progmgr@nekwmd.org

Universal Recycling Law – Act 148

As of July 1, 2015 the following recyclables are banned from landfills in Vermont. Materials must be REASONABLY CLEAN and uncontaminated to be RECYCLABLE!

– Aluminum & Steel Cans– Aluminum Foil & Pie Pans– Glass Bottles & Jars from Food & Beverages– Plastic Bottles, Jugs & Tubs marked #1, & #2– Corrugated Cardboard– White & Colored Paper– Newspaper, Magazines, Catalogs, Junk Mail, Paper Envelopes – Boxboard (grey, non-corrugated cardboard – like cereal boxes)

These are the mandated recyclables –Glover Recycling accepts these and other recyclable materials.

NO: Couches, Chairs, Mattresses, Rugs, or Tires. These items, except tires, MUST go to Casella at 21 Landfill Lane Coventry, VT 802 334-8300

FOOD SCRAPSVermont law now requires that food scraps be composted – not sent to the landfill.Glover Recycling accepts the following food types:

Meat & BonesMilk, cheese, other dairy productsNuts & shellsOils & fatsEggs, egg shells soups, sauces, condiments, herbs, spices Flour, breads, pastasSeafood & shells

Please remove all plastic stickers from fruit & veg skins – they do not compost. Tea bags and coffee filters are the only acceptable paper products.NO “COMPOSTABLE” PLASTIC BAGS!No commercially grown flowers – they contain preservatives.

THERE IS NO CHARGE FOR RECYCLING IN GLOVER!

TRASH COLLECTION AT GLOVER RECYCLING

Bagged Trash PRICE CHANGE: September 1, 2025

Kitchen Size Bag: $3

30 Gallon Bag: $5

Contractor Bag: $8

# RIVER Property Concerns with Rivers and Streams After Recent Flooding

- Source URL: https://townofglover.com/river/
- Final URL: https://townofglover.com/river/
- Crawled: 2026-07-30T19:08:31.913755+00:00
- Page type: page
- Published/updated: 2024-05-22T18:24:38+00:00 2024-11-05T14:47:09+00:00

## Page content

### Resilience Initiative for Vermont Empowerment and Recovery (RIVER)

https://riverprojectsvt.org

LATEST NEWS

Glover Officials Deal With Landslide Near Former Fire Station

### Glover Village Aerial Photos

### Dams

### Flood Damage

## Property Concerns with Rivers and Streams After Recent Flooding

Montpelier, Vt. – Recent flooding has altered Vermont’s landscape and property owners understandably have questions. The Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC) has prepared answers to common questions:

##### Q: Recent flooding moved the stream/river extremely close to my home/business. Will the state come and fix it?

A: If you feel your home or business is unsafe, take necessary measures to protect your safety, including leaving the building.

If you think work is needed immediately to stabilize the river, you may hire a contractor to do the work as an emergency protective measure, under authorization of the town. Contact your town to alert them of the issue, as they are required to report within 72 hours. A DEC River Management Engineer will get there as soon as their schedule allows. There may be work required at a later date if emergency work further destabilizes the river.

If you feel work is needed to stabilize the river but there is not an immediate threat, please send your name, email address, phone number, and full address including town name to anr.wsmdrivers@vermont.gov. A DEC River Management Engineer will contact you as soon as their schedule allows. They will work with you to schedule a visit to assess your property and advise you on work.

The DEC River Management Section is not a funding program but can help you determine the appropriate scope of work that meets state regulations.

##### Q: Will someone remove the wood and debris in the river near my property?

A: If the wood or debris is changing or redirecting the flow of the river and immediately threatening homes or businesses, you may hire a contractor to do the work to stabilize the river as an emergency protective measure under authorization of the town. Alternatively, towns have the authority to implement emergency protective measures to protect public infrastructure and public safety. Contact your town to alert them of the issue.

Emergency protective measures need to be reported within 72 hours. A DEC River Management Engineer will get there as soon as their schedule allows. There may be work required at a later date if emergency work further destabilizes the river or impacts adjacent infrastructure.

##### Q: My home has been damaged or destroyed by recent flooding. What do I do next and what assistance is available?

A: Information and resources are available at https://floodready.vermont.gov/help-after-flooding.

##### Q: My town road is washed out next to my property. When will it be fixed?

A: Contact your town/highway department or road foreman to alert them of the issue. Towns are responsible for repairs to town roads. DEC River Management Engineers work closely with town officials to ensure repairs meet state standards.

##### Q: Who will stop the heavy equipment from destroying the river?

A: Flood events require work within rivers and streams to protect and repair human investments and related infrastructure. Towns have the authority to implement emergency protective measures to protect public safety.

The DEC Rivers Program regulates activities in rivers and streams to ensure that work does not create additional flood hazards or cause damage to fish habitat.

The most common issue after a flood is over-dredging of rivers or excessive streambank filling. While limited excavations and streambank stabilization may be needed to maintain river channel capacity and protect investments, over-dredging or over-filling creates a much more unstable river which threatens adjacent property and infrastructure during the next flood.

DEC may require a permit and follow-up work at a later date if deemed necessary for a safe river condition or restoration of habitat.

You may report concerns regarding work in rivers to anr.wsmdrivers@vermont.gov. Please provide location information including name of town, name of river/stream, and nearest address and/or crossroads.

##### Q: Is there financial assistance for me to stabilize the streambank on my property?

A: The Emergency Watershed Protection grant program administered by the U.S. Natural Resources Conservation Service provides financial assistance for this type of work.

For more information on flood recovery resources from the Agency of Natural Resources, Department of Environmental Conservation, Fish and Wildlife Department, or the Department of Forests, Parks, and Recreation, visit https://ANR.Vermont.gov/Flood.

## Page content

Glover Town Clerk’s Office 51 Bean Hill Glover, VT 05839 phone (802)525-6227 fax (802)525-4115 HOURS: 7:00 am – 5:00 pm Monday – Thursday Closed Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays, and Holidays

### Glover Selectboard Meetings

Selectboard Meetings have moved to the Town Hall. Regular selectboard meetings are held on the 2nd and 4th Thursdays of the month at 6:30 pm.

##### Glover Recycling Information. SUMMER HOURS: Starts April 1 – November 30.

HOURS: Wednesday: Noon – 3pm Saturday: 9am – Noon

PLEASE:

- Sort materials at home so you can limit time at Recycling
- Please WEAR a MASK if you are not vaccinated
- Keep your distance from Attendants and other Recyclers
- Bring correct change for trash payment if possible
- CLICK HERE FOR LIST OF RECYCLABLES

# 2026 Glover Town Plan Community Survey

- Source URL: https://townofglover.com/2026-glover-town-plan-community-survey/
- Final URL: https://townofglover.com/2026-glover-town-plan-community-survey/
- Crawled: 2026-07-30T19:05:02.734801+00:00
- Page type: post
- Published/updated: 2025-03-20T12:21:39+00:00 2025-03-20T12:21:39+00:00 2025-03-20T12:21:39+00:00 2025-11-26T23:21:45+00:00 2026-02-03T21:35:53+00:00 2025-12-08T12:31:26+00:00 2025-03-12T14:08:57+00:00 2023-07-20T13:32:37+00:00 2025-08-29T18:23:43+00:00

## Page content

Every eight years, our community comes together to rethink and refresh the Glover Town Plan. The current plan, last reviewed in 2018, is due for completion by the end of 2026. Why is this so important? A clear and well-structured Town Plan is a practical roadmap for shaping our collective future. It also opens the door to valuable resources—by articulating our goals and concerns, Glover becomes more likely to receive grants and assistance to help bring these visions to life.

Crafting a Town Plan involves taking an honest look at our hometown—honoring our history, pinpointing our strengths and areas that need attention, and envisioning the possibilities ahead. This survey is a vital first step in that process. Your input will help identify priorities, refine objectives, and drive meaningful projects in coordination with neighboring towns and regional plans.

To ensure everyone has an opportunity to participate, the survey will remain open through the end of March 2025.

If you have questions, you may contact a member of the Selectboard or a member of the Planning Commission. Please go to the Town of Glover website for contact information.

As a thank-you, all participants who provide contact information will be entered into a raffle for a chance to win one of two $25 Currier’s/C&C gift cards or a $25 Parker Pie gift card. Your perspective matters—let’s shape Glover’s future together!

# A LATE THANK YOU!

- Page type: post

## Page content

Sorry for the delayed thank you to everyone who helped put the chairs and tables back into the town hall.

This week new front steps went in and the bathroom will soon be ready to paint.

Again, Thanks to all who came out and to those who let us borrow their trailers.

Theresa Perron

# Auction – May 10th

- Source URL: https://townofglover.com/auction-may-10th/
- Final URL: https://townofglover.com/auction-may-10th/
- Crawled: 2026-07-30T19:05:10.457402+00:00
- Page type: post
- Published/updated: 2025-04-17T13:26:02+00:00 2025-04-29T11:55:56+00:00 2025-04-17T13:26:02+00:00 2025-04-29T11:55:56+00:00 2023-09-07T12:31:24+00:00 2025-03-19T13:58:55+00:00 2026-06-01T18:39:11+00:00 2024-02-20T18:32:14+00:00 2026-06-01T14:23:38+00:00 2025-12-08T12:15:39+00:00

## Page content

Auction Items Needed!

Auction – May 10th, join us for potluck at 5 p.m. auction starts at 6 p.m.

Do you own a business and could you donate a gift certificate to a worthy cause? Do you have talent, are you an artist and have art to donate? Do you grow beautiful plants? Is it time to purge items you no longer need or use? We are looking for good, useful items for our SLD Auction. Maybe you could donate a cord of wood, or a truck load of stone, a gift basket of home-raised meat items, they would make a good auction item! EGGS! – We all love fresh eggs! Be creative with your items – make a gift basket of home-baked goods. Do you do yearly canning? – Create a gift basket of jellies, jams or pickles. Doughnuts, fresh baked bread, pies and cookies all make great items to auction off. Are you a business that could donate gift certificates? Have you been looking for a home for those used furnishings? – We can help.Drop off items on May 9th from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. at the Glover Town Hall or Mail your Gift Certificates to Town of Glover, 51 Bean Hill Road, Glover, VT 05839 Att: Shadow Lake Dam.

Please call for questions or to inform us of your donation at 802 525-7199 or email: theresa@townofglover.comHelp Save The Shadow Lake Dam! shadowlakedam.org

The Glover Bicentennial Scholarship is available to any Glover resident, both graduating seniorsor adult learners, who wish to continue their education. Applications are available at the TownClerk’s office or the high school with an April 30, 2024 deadline.

# Call For Cleanup Volunteers

- Source URL: https://townofglover.com/call-for-cleanup-volunteers/
- Final URL: https://townofglover.com/call-for-cleanup-volunteers/
- Crawled: 2026-07-30T19:05:23.932317+00:00
- Page type: post
- Published/updated: 2023-07-12T17:06:41+00:00 2023-07-12T17:11:37+00:00 2023-07-12T17:06:41+00:00 2023-07-12T17:11:37+00:00 2026-04-22T15:37:33+00:00 2026-05-18T12:51:41+00:00 2026-02-03T21:35:53+00:00 2026-01-12T12:17:00+00:00 2023-09-15T12:03:38+00:00 2023-09-22T12:06:56+00:00 2026-05-18T12:50:46+00:00

## Page content

The flood waters have receded from the basement of the Town Hall have receded, leaving the floor and many low-placed its covered in mud. There is still a lot of moisture in the basement, and we need more fans and dehumidifiers. If anyone has any to loan, please bring them to the Town Hall as soon as you can. We could also use help cleaning the tables that were in the basement and loading them into the elevator to move them upstairs. Once we have a dumpster, we may need help removing other items from the basement as well. If you can help, email leanne@townofglover.com or just come on down to the Town Hall today.

## Page content

At its October 14th regular meeting, the Glover Select Board approved the creation of an Equity Committee charged with the task recommending a Declaration of Inclusion for the board to adopt and with making recommendations to the board for how it can promote and sustain equity, inclusion and diversity in the town of Glover. If you are a resident of Glover, committed to these values and want to serve on this committee, e-mail bcarrollgloversb@comcast.net.

# Drought Task Force

- Source URL: https://townofglover.com/drought-task-force/
- Final URL: https://townofglover.com/drought-task-force/
- Crawled: 2026-07-30T19:05:39.686727+00:00
- Page type: post
- Published/updated: 2025-09-19T15:48:11+00:00 2025-09-19T15:48:11+00:00 2025-09-19T15:48:11+00:00 2024-10-21T13:53:58+00:00 2024-09-16T13:01:48+00:00 2024-10-16T16:07:27+00:00 2024-10-15T16:09:29+00:00 2023-07-20T13:04:18+00:00 2024-02-22T13:26:41+00:00 2025-01-10T11:02:23+00:00 2025-02-03T12:42:25+00:00 2025-09-15T12:19:02+00:00 2025-10-03T12:30:26+00:00

## Page content

As many towns are aware, Vermont is currently experiencing widespread drought conditions and as a result VEM Director Forand has activated the State EOC to enhanced operations and a multi-agency Drought Task Force has been established to help provide coordination and support. The Agency of Natural Resources has created a drought resources page: Drought Resources | Agency of Natural Resources (https://anr.vermont.gov/disaster/drought) which provides information about conditions, water haulers, and a place to share impacts to individuals, water systems, and agricultural businesses. We are encouraging the reporting of any issues so that the state has situational awareness of impacts.

The National Weather Services is not forecasting any significant rainfall in the short term so conditions are expected to persist at least into next week. There is some indication that we may see some rainfall in the middle of next week but probably not enough to make any significant dent in the overall drought. On top of drought conditions, we continue to deal with high wildfire danger. Those conditions will also likely persist until we get some soaking rainfall. You can find information on wildfire conditions here: Monitoring Fire Danger | Department of Forests, Parks and Recreation (https://fpr.vermont.gov/forest/wildland-fire/monitoring-fire-danger).

As always, if you have any questions, please feel free to reach out to me. If you need emergency assistance, our Watch Officer can be reached 24/7 at 1-800-347-0488. Just as a side note, that number goes to a VSP answering point after business hours and they may answer as the Hazmat Line, or Spill Line, just let them know you’re calling for the watch officer.

Zachary Borst | Regional Coordinator – Orleans, Essex, CaledoniaVermont Emergency Management

# Emergency Management Director

- Source URL: https://townofglover.com/emergency-management-director/
- Final URL: https://townofglover.com/emergency-management-director/
- Crawled: 2026-07-30T19:05:41.770244+00:00
- Page type: post
- Published/updated: 2023-07-20T12:25:55+00:00 2023-07-20T12:25:55+00:00 2023-07-20T12:25:55+00:00 2026-06-26T18:56:25+00:00 2026-01-12T12:18:37+00:00 2026-07-07T19:17:24+00:00 2024-09-10T18:16:55+00:00 2026-07-01T11:09:45+00:00 2026-03-10T13:38:25+00:00

## Page content

CALL 211 TO REPORT DAMAGE / POTABLE WATER AVAILABLE IN GLOVER

July 19, 2020 Glover Residents;

The last 10 days or so have been a trying time for some of our residents. The flooding on July 10th along the Barton River in Glover Village as well as other locations in town has turned the everyday lives of some of our residents upside down.

FEMA ASSISTANCE:

At the Thursday, July 13th selectboard meeting I was appointed Emergency Management Director for the Town of Glover. This past Monday was spent walking through Glover Village with representatives from FEMA (Federal Emergency Management Agency), the US Small Business Administration, and Vermont Emergency Management. As many have found out thus far, Orleans County has NOT been declared eligible for INDIVIDUAL assistance from FEMA. The purpose of the tour with those agencies was to assess the overall damage so that Orleans County CAN be added to the list of six other counties where individuals will be eligible for help from FEMA. To that extent, it is IMPERATIVE that ANYONE with damage, call 211 to report that. Vermont 211 is acting as the repository for reporting damage. The more reports to 211 from those suffering damage will assist in providing the required documentation to get Orleans County declared eligible for INDIVIDUAL assistance from FEMA. I can’t stress enough: PLEASE CALL 211 TO REPORT ANY DAMAGE, NO MATTER HOW MINIMAL YOU THINK IT MAY BE! Also, any damage outside of Glover Village should be reported to 211 as well; it is not just Village residents who should report damage. At this time we are unsure of if/when a declaration will come.

DRINKING WATER SAFETY:

https://www.healthvermont.gov/environment/drinking-water/after-flood-private-drinking-water-guidance

The above link outlines drinking water safety after a flood for private drinking water sources such as springs and wells. The Town of Glover has received a supply of bottled drinking water that is available for distribution for those that have either lost their source of potable water or their water remains untested/unsafe to drink. Please contact the town clerk’s office at (802) 525-6227 or contact the town Emergency Management Director at (802) 673-4030 for more information on how to obtain drinking water.

As we progress with recovery efforts, we will post updates to the Town of Glover Facebook page and the town website.

SincerelyPhilip Brooks, Emergency Management Director Town of Glover

## Page content

Town of Glover has limited access in or out. Rt 16 and all tributary roads are washed out.

Fire and EMS are out evacuating those that are stranded.

In the mean time, a shelter has been set up at the Glover Fire Station at 63 Bean Hill.

# From the Vermont Emergency Management, Dept of Public Safety

- Source URL: https://townofglover.com/from-the-vermont-emergency-management-dept-of-public-safety/
- Final URL: https://townofglover.com/from-the-vermont-emergency-management-dept-of-public-safety/
- Crawled: 2026-07-30T19:05:47.005684+00:00
- Page type: post
- Published/updated: 2023-08-02T12:49:18+00:00 2023-08-02T12:49:18+00:00 2023-08-02T12:49:18+00:00 2023-08-02T12:43:28+00:00 2025-01-27T13:21:40+00:00 2025-10-29T12:03:03+00:00 2025-11-17T15:56:37+00:00 2026-06-26T18:43:43+00:00 2026-06-26T18:55:27+00:00 2026-06-23T18:09:31+00:00 2026-06-23T19:07:08+00:00 2026-02-10T21:06:42+00:00 2023-07-25T12:37:28+00:00

## Page content

- Disaster Recovery Center (DRC) location announced: FEMA will open a DRC for Orleans Co in Barton’s Memorial Hall, 17 Village Square, beginning tomorrow, 8/2/23 at 1pm. Regular hours are Mon-Sun (daily!) from 8a to 7p.
- Transportation to DRC: We’ve submitted a request to authorize RTC to supply on-demand transportation to Orleans Co DRC, as they’re doing in Johnson and Hardwick areas. Stay tuned.
- Property Buyouts Info: the simplest way for a citizen to inquire about buyouts is to complete VEM’s intake form here: VEM Buyout Intake Form (there are multiple funding streams for buyouts, so this is definitely the way to go!)
- Debris Removal: Towns are responsible for a plan to remove flood-related debris for residents/businesses. Individual Debris Allowance: FEMA is offering up to $300 for flood clean-up work in damaged but habitable homes. The Clean and Sanitize Assistance program can be accessed online at the FEMA site, by calling 800-621-3362, and possibly by asking at the DRC.
- Towns are responsible for a plan to remove flood-related debris for residents/businesses.
- Individual Debris Allowance: FEMA is offering up to $300 for flood clean-up work in damaged but habitable homes. The Clean and Sanitize Assistance program can be accessed online at the FEMA site, by calling 800-621-3362, and possibly by asking at the DRC.
- FEMA County Coordinator: FEMA has named the County Coordinator who will be a “front door” for town questions. Nadia Tash has met with several of you already and will share how you can utilize her to the best advantage.

- Crawled: 2026-07-30T19:06:01.747903+00:00

- Published/updated: 2022-06-23T17:37:00+00:00 2022-08-24T13:14:55+00:00 2022-06-23T17:37:00+00:00 2022-08-24T13:14:55+00:00 2025-11-11T13:34:14+00:00 2023-11-21T12:22:53+00:00 2026-01-28T20:35:52+00:00 2026-05-21T22:13:24+00:00 2026-02-16T14:10:28+00:00 2026-06-01T14:21:45+00:00

## Page content

The Glover Cemetery Commission is offering two new burial options at the Westlook II Cemetery, hopefully by this fall: (1) a green/natural burial section, and (2) a memorial garden. On Wednesday, June 29 at 7 PM at the Glover Town Hall, the commission will be sharing the plans for both options. All are invited to attend.

## Page content

Wednesday, August 13, 6:30 – 7:30 p.m.

Glover Town Hall

GCT is a group of community residents coming together to consider available properties to purchase, renovate, and create housing opportunities, through grants and fundraising.

Other possibilities for these properties are an option. GCT is open to ideas and conversations.

Come join this small group and help build a safe, vibrant, productive community for all.

Interested? Need more info? Email Barb Delzio at barbdelzio@gmail.com

## Page content

Are you a student looking to earn extra money this summer? Or a retiree with an interest in preserving our ecosystems? The Glover Recycling Center seeks a part-attendant, starting in August. You’ll stay busy, meet and greet your community and make a difference with very little stress, Contact brian@townofglover.com for details.

Brian F. Carroll, Town Administrator Town of Glover, Vermont 802.673.7149

# Glover Town Administrator Job Advertisement

- Source URL: https://townofglover.com/glover-town-administratorjob-advertisement/
- Final URL: https://townofglover.com/glover-town-administratorjob-advertisement/
- Crawled: 2026-07-30T19:07:34.236253+00:00
- Page type: post
- Published/updated: 2023-01-27T14:04:58+00:00 2023-01-27T15:10:53+00:00 2023-01-27T14:04:58+00:00 2023-01-27T15:10:53+00:00 2026-06-01T14:29:58+00:00 2026-05-12T00:43:56+00:00 2025-12-16T20:39:34+00:00 2025-12-17T12:58:48+00:00 2023-07-11T15:52:29+00:00 2025-10-27T22:05:29+00:00 2026-02-16T14:02:23+00:00

## Page content

Position: Glover Town Administrator

The town of Glover seeks a Town Administrator, a newly created position to support both functions of the Town Clerk/Treasurer’s office and the Town’s Select Board. This position will report to the Town Clerk/Treasurer and the Chair of the Glover Select Board. Along with a good sense of humor, ideal candidate should be well organized, possess strong communication skills, have basic experience and knowledge related to municipal government, board policy, accounting practices, tax procurement, land recordings, social media, general elections and public meetings management, among other general duties. Experience with the municipal accounting program, NEMRC, is desired.

Interested parties should contact brian@townofglover.com for an application for submission along with a resume and (3) letters of reference to either Cindy@townofglover.com or David@townofglover.com. Glover is an equal opportunity employer.

# Insulating Window Inserts

- Source URL: https://townofglover.com/insulating-window-inserts-2/
- Final URL: https://townofglover.com/insulating-window-inserts-2/
- Crawled: 2026-07-30T19:07:46.139554+00:00
- Page type: post
- Published/updated: 2024-09-11T12:03:06+00:00 2024-09-11T12:03:49+00:00 2024-09-11T12:03:06+00:00 2024-09-11T12:03:49+00:00 2026-07-13T21:01:45+00:00 2023-08-16T14:29:43+00:00 2024-02-22T13:26:00+00:00 2025-10-15T12:51:11+00:00 2025-02-19T17:41:59+00:00 2026-07-13T21:07:29+00:00 2023-08-08T15:13:56+00:00

## Page content

Glover Energy Committee will be offering WindowDressers insulating window inserts again in 2024. The inserts are custom fit interior storm windows – a pine frame wrapped on each side with a heat-shrink plastic film. They greatly reduce heat loss through windows and save money on fuel while making homes more comfortable. They are custom measured to fit each window and assembled in community workshops by volunteers – which help keep prices reasonable. Up to 10 inserts are available for free for households with limited income.

Reply to this posting for more information, or call 802 525-4277, or go to WindowDressers website: https://windowdressers.org/ and click on the inserts tab. Inserts will be assembled in Glover in early November, 2024.

## Page content

Are you a student looking for some extra cash? A retiree looking for a busy but low stress job? The Town of Glover is looking for a responsible person to work in its Recycling Program, maximum 6 hours per week. Hourly wage is $15.00 an hour. Interested parties can contact theresa@townofglover.com for an application or stop by the Town Clerks Office in Glover.

—Theresa PerronTown Administrator/Assistant Town ClerkTown of Glover, Vermont 802-525-6227

- Page type: post
- Published/updated: 2025-07-07T12:51:17+00:00 2025-07-07T12:51:17+00:00 2025-07-07T12:51:17+00:00 2024-12-19T13:25:45+00:00 2025-09-22T15:01:03+00:00 2026-02-11T22:26:40+00:00 2025-05-05T13:33:58+00:00 2025-05-08T14:00:58+00:00 2025-02-19T17:41:59+00:00 2026-02-16T14:07:17+00:00

## Page content

### TOWN of GLOVER FLOOD ZONE & RIVER CORRIDOR BYLAW UPDATE

The Town of Glover is beginning the process of updating the 1991 Flood Hazard Area Regulation as required by FEMA. A draft of the proposed new Flood Hazard and River Corridor Bylaw can be seen on the town’s website: https://townofglover.com/draft-flood-hazard-river-corridor-bylaw/.

Drafting and adoption of a new bylaw is a long process and must be finished by 2027. The Planning Commission will hold an Open Forum on Thursday, July 17, 2025 at the Town Hall at 6:30 pm to present the draft bylaw, hear comments, and answer questions from Glover property owners. This will be the second public meeting on the topic.

The purpose of the proposed Flood Zone and River Corridor Bylaw is to control future development in the flood zone and river corridors in an attempt to give rivers and streams the room they need when water flows are high and thereby help reduce damage in future flooding events.

Flooding in Glover in July 2023 and 2024 and damage to homes, businesses and infrastructure were a strong reminder that areas of Glover are prone to flooding. The 1991 Flood Regulation now in force must be updated so that properties in the Glover flood zone will continue to be eligible for the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP).

Regulation of development in river corridors is not required by FEMA but is encouraged by the State of Vermont. More information is available on the state’s Flood Ready website: floodready.vermont.gov/

If you own property in the flood zone in Glover Village, in a flood-prone lakeshore area, along the Barton River, or along any stream that runs year-round, please come to the Open Forum on Thursday, July 17, 2025 at the Town Hall at 6:30 pm.

Online attendance through Zoom is available but please attend in person if possible:

https://us06web.zoom.us/j/82434214972

Glover Planning Commission

- Published/updated: 2025-08-06T17:30:01+00:00 2025-08-06T17:30:01+00:00 2025-08-06T17:30:01+00:00 2024-03-26T11:24:32+00:00 2026-07-14T10:59:54+00:00 2025-12-03T22:09:04+00:00 2025-11-11T13:34:14+00:00 2026-06-25T20:47:24+00:00 2026-01-06T20:51:06+00:00

## Page content

Memphremagog Watershed Association and Northwoods Stewardship Center Conservation crew will begin the excavation of the planned areas. Reilly Auger will be excavating – Mike Pray and crew will be supplying Grant required In-Kind Services to support Reilly.

There will be two opportunities to help with digging and planting existing flowers at the Municipal Building (Town Clerk’s Office). It is a great opportunity to be part of the Glover Rain Gardens.

On August 22, 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. we will dig up plants and clean the roots of those plants, so as not to capture the invasive vine and weeds, then re-pot to save for the planting day, which will be August 29.

You can save a slip for your own personal gardens if you wish. It is important to know that the mint is very invasive. You should put it in a container or where you do not mind it taking over.

Some of these plants will be used near the bridge area and some in the gardens.

We gathered lupin seeds and another seed yesterday and they will be processed for the new gardens.

If there is time to spare, it would be great to clean up the tree line of the invasive vine and misc. debris. It is very overgrown and could use some care. Bring Clippers for this.

On August 29th, 10 a.m. to 2 p.m, we will be planting new plants from Kate Butler along with the seeds that were gathered and the plants we set aside.

Please let me know if you are interested in being here. Please share with anyone who would like to help.

Tell me which days you can help out. Please respond.

Bring tools (mark them) of your choice, gloves, lunch, and water.

If you have left over pots from summer planting bring those!

See attached below agreement.

A section of Parker Road will be closed on Wednesday, July 19, 2023, near Dennis Gibson’s, in order to repair the culvert near the bridge. We anticipate the road being closed between 8am – Noon.

Thank you for your patience.

# Rabies Notice 9/8/2025

- Source URL: https://townofglover.com/rabies-notice-9-8-2025/
- Final URL: https://townofglover.com/rabies-notice-9-8-2025/
- Crawled: 2026-07-30T19:08:25.901813+00:00
- Page type: post
- Published/updated: 2025-09-09T12:01:18+00:00 2025-09-09T12:01:18+00:00 2025-09-09T12:01:18+00:00 2025-09-19T15:48:11+00:00 2024-02-20T17:02:08+00:00 2024-02-22T13:25:18+00:00 2025-07-01T16:45:25+00:00 2025-05-05T13:33:58+00:00 2025-05-08T14:00:58+00:00 2024-02-22T13:24:48+00:00 2024-02-26T20:08:55+00:00 2024-09-16T13:01:48+00:00

## Page content

The Health Department noted a recent case of rabies in a raccoon in the town of Glover, Vermont. Since wild animals move and interact with each other, a rabid animal detection means there is circulation of the virus and a risk of rabies from wildlife in the greater town area. All residents are urged to take steps to protect humans and domestic animals from rabies.

If you are bitten by an animal: wash the wound very well with soap and water and contact your health care provider. Follow all their instructions.

If your pet or farm animal was exposed to a wild or stray animal that might have rabies: contact your veterinarian. State law requires dogs and cats to be vaccinated for rabies — even barn cats.

If you see a wild or stray animal acting strangely, or are concerned about a rabies exposure, call the Rabies Hotline (1-800-4-RABIES) or report it to your town’s animal control officer. 1st Constable: Job Breitmeyer 802-323-6092 or 802-525-1305, 2nd Constable: Cindy Epinette 802-525-6227 or 802-525-5550, Health Officer: Anne Eldridge 802-363-2688.

Do not touch or pick up wild or stray animals – even baby animals – or try to make them into pets. Doing so can put yourself or your family at risk of exposure through a bite or scratch. You can’t tell if an animal has rabies just by looking at it. Interacting with young wildlife may result in them being orphaned or tested for rabies, which requires humanely euthanizing the animal. So, for their own sake, leave wildlife in the wild.

Learn more about rabies in Vermont – visit www.healthvermont.gov/rabies.

Rabies is a deadly viral disease of the brain that infects mammals and is fatal to both humans and animals. In Vermont, rabies is most commonly found in wild animals such as raccoons, skunks, foxes, bats and woodchucks. Cats, dogs and livestock can also get rabies if they have not been vaccinated. Rabies virus is spread through the bite of an infected animal. Rabies is transmitted when the virus is introduced into a bite wound, open cuts on the skin, or onto mucous membranes like the mouth or eyes.

802 525-7199 OR 802 624-3463

## Page content

Thank you to everyone who has been vigilant about sending us photographs and reporting property damage. Even if you have already cleaned up, we also request that you report any damage to the state hotline by calling 211. The more reports out of Glover that they receive help us with a better chance of getting FEMA assistance.

Thank you for your patience.

# Road Update after Flood

- Source URL: https://townofglover.com/road-update-after-flood/
- Final URL: https://townofglover.com/road-update-after-flood/
- Crawled: 2026-07-30T19:08:34.474782+00:00
- Page type: post
- Published/updated: 2023-07-11T15:52:29+00:00 2023-07-11T15:52:29+00:00 2023-07-11T15:52:29+00:00 2026-03-10T13:18:54+00:00 2025-10-28T21:08:22+00:00 2023-07-20T12:37:23+00:00 2026-06-26T18:56:25+00:00 2025-07-07T12:51:17+00:00 2026-04-09T16:59:27+00:00

## Page content

The town of Glover hopes that everyone is staying safe. Here is what we know about local roads so far:

Dexter Road Closed

King Road Closed past Tatro Lane, may be possible with a pickup but we don’t recommend it

The 4-corners of Stevens Road is washed out past the Barton line

County Road in Albany is washed out

Craftsbury remains cut off from everywhere except through Shadow Lake

Due to our other responsibilities in responding to flooding, we may not be able to continually provide updates about roads on social media throughout the day. Unfortunately, there is not coordinated communication between towns at the moment to provide a comprehensive state-wide update about roads outside of our town. However, more information can be obtained by joining the “VT Flooding 2023 Response and Recovery Mutual Aid“ Facebook page.

Thanks, Leanne

## Page content

Due to flood damage, tonight’s Select Board Meeting will take place in the back room at the Glover Fire Department, beginning at 6:45. This will be an in-person meeting only, with no hybrid option to attend online. We regret any inconvenience that this might cause, but made this decision out of concern for the health and safety of our community members.

## Page content

The Glover Select Board would like to express disappointment and apologies to those who attempted to access the February meetings remotely. Due to some technical difficulties, we were unable to make the critical connections. Rest assured, we have been working on solving the glitches and will be prepared to offer Town Meeting access under a remote/hybrid format on March 7th. Please be aware that, if you do choose to access remotely, you will not be eligible for voting on the presented articles.

# Shadow Lake Beach is now handicapped accessible for those using wheelchairs and walkers

- Source URL: https://townofglover.com/shadow-lake-beach-is-now-handicapped-accessible-for-those-using-wheelchairs-and-walkers/
- Final URL: https://townofglover.com/shadow-lake-beach-is-now-handicapped-accessible-for-those-using-wheelchairs-and-walkers/
- Crawled: 2026-07-30T19:10:10.013447+00:00
- Page type: post
- Published/updated: 2023-08-08T15:13:56+00:00 2023-08-08T15:13:56+00:00 2023-08-08T15:13:56+00:00 2026-06-23T18:09:31+00:00 2026-06-23T19:07:08+00:00 2025-05-13T11:22:36+00:00 2025-06-17T12:32:41+00:00 2025-11-26T23:21:45+00:00 2026-05-19T15:02:52+00:00 2026-07-13T21:06:00+00:00 2026-07-13T21:01:45+00:00

## Page content

A 133′ Mobimat, five feet wide, has been laid from the left side of the parking lot down to the water, and extends into the water to about three feet in depth, with the end marked with a floating noodle. A submersible wheel chair is attached to the fence near the parking lot with a bicycle cable and combination lock. Phone the Town Clerk’s Office to get the combination. 802 525-6227

Anyone going into the water in the wheelchair needs to have an assistant with them. Bring your own cushion and a strap to secure yourself in the wheelchair.

The Town of Glover is using ARPA funds to make this much needed improvement to our public beach. Please give us your feedback, so we can get this arranged in the best way for our friends who need it to access the water.

The entire parking lot in front of the beach is reserved for handicapped and mobility challenged patrons. If you are able bodied, please park in the lot across the road.

Dennis Gibson, Peggy Day Gibson and Diane Rodgers secured the mat to the beach. It will be rolled back up before winter.

## Page content

Weston & Sampson begin their analysis on the Shadow Lake Dam starting the week of, (12/9/24). Please be respectful with the workers as they do their work and do not enter the property while they are there.

You can find more information at https://shadowlakedam.org/ including video and photos as they come available. Contact Theresa Perron with questions: 802 525-7199.

- Crawled: 2026-07-30T19:10:17.012865+00:00
- Page type: post
- Published/updated: 2023-07-11T22:16:56+00:00 2023-07-11T22:16:56+00:00 2023-07-11T22:16:56+00:00 2025-12-24T14:38:36+00:00 2026-01-28T12:38:01+00:00 2026-02-19T18:38:07+00:00 2026-06-25T22:00:32+00:00 2026-02-27T21:33:28+00:00 2025-10-01T16:55:00+00:00

## Page content

The Glover Selectboard is inviting residents of Glover to send their photographs of storm damage to us. We are collecting photographs for both awareness of storm damage in our town, as well as historical record, and would like to have all photographs go to a single email address created just for organizing this collection. Please send your photographs to gloverstormdamage2023@gmail.com, along with a brief description of where in Glover the photograph was taken and any other information that you think is important.

# Special Town Meeting – June 14, 2025 Will include discussion of new Flood Zone & River Corridor Bylaws

- Source URL: https://townofglover.com/special-town-meeting-june-14-2025-will-include-discussion-of-new-flood-zone-river-corridor-bylaws/
- Final URL: https://townofglover.com/special-town-meeting-june-14-2025-will-include-discussion-of-new-flood-zone-river-corridor-bylaws/
- Crawled: 2026-07-30T19:10:37.788711+00:00
- Page type: post
- Published/updated: 2025-05-30T15:06:13+00:00 2025-06-17T12:31:48+00:00 2025-05-30T15:06:13+00:00 2025-06-17T12:31:48+00:00 2024-01-30T15:02:15+00:00 2026-06-11T16:05:42+00:00 2026-06-17T18:49:23+00:00 2026-03-09T11:05:31+00:00 2026-06-01T14:23:38+00:00 2026-01-12T12:17:50+00:00

## Page content

The Glover Planning Commission and Select board are considering mandatory updates to the Glover Flood Hazard Area Regulation and the possible addition of a River Corridor Bylaw.There will be time at the end of the SPECIAL TOWN MEETING on SATURDAY, June 14, 2025 for discussion and questions regarding these changes.Please attend the June 14, 10:00 AM Special Town Meeting, at the TOWN HALLto learn more about these changes.Reminder: the 1991 Flood Area Regulation is in effect. Any development in the Flood Hazard Area requires a permit. Permit applications are available at the Town Office.

- Published/updated: 2023-07-13T15:45:27+00:00 2023-07-13T15:45:27+00:00 2023-07-13T15:45:27+00:00 2026-06-18T17:35:58+00:00 2026-05-21T22:13:24+00:00 2026-03-09T11:17:25+00:00 2025-10-28T12:27:35+00:00 2026-06-23T18:17:34+00:00 2026-06-24T13:40:20+00:00 2026-02-19T13:46:59+00:00 2026-02-19T13:55:48+00:00

## Page content

Please be aware that the lakes and ponds in Glover have not been tested yet, and swimming is at your own risk. We are currently seeking further guidance. We hope to provide further information soon. We are testing now, and will be testing again on Monday after the next upcoming rainstorms, but again, do not advise swimming at this time.

- Published/updated: 2023-07-18T22:19:41+00:00 2023-07-18T22:19:41+00:00 2023-07-18T22:19:41+00:00 2025-05-19T11:52:47+00:00 2026-03-10T13:38:25+00:00 2025-06-30T13:29:49+00:00 2025-12-24T14:40:01+00:00 2023-07-25T15:47:31+00:00 2024-11-06T13:19:16+00:00

## Page content

The Town of Glover was amazed at the outpouring of support for the Senior Meal Site and the Town Hall facility in a clean-up effort after the flood. The downstairs of the town hall sustained a considerable amount of water and mud damage affecting not only the hall itself but the contents of the meal site. Many came to help inventory the affected food content and dispose of damaged goods. Helping hands washed and sanitized all furniture, shelves and pots and pans and dishes, then moved everything to be temporarily stored in the upstairs of the hall.

We would like to list all who came and gave a helping hand. Patsy Tompkins – Director of the senior meals, Richard Jesmer – Assistant Director, Donna Greenwood – Meal Prep., Meghan Wayland, Ally Howell, Terese Perron, Joan Alexander, Paul Curino, Mary Anne Royer, Tina Ghantous, Nila Mahar, Randy Williams, Heidi Ecker-Racz, Kate Wolf, Liz Nelson, Mike Reddy, Hillary Savage, Tom Jesmer, Jeremy & Leanne Harple, Heidi Riendeau and Kelsey. I apologize if your name was inadvertently omitted. Special thanks for those who brought fans and dehumidifiers that are still in use.

Again, thank you and it could not have been accomplished without you. We still have a lot of work to do. The sheet rock and insulation were removed and will need to be replaced and there is still more to be removed. We need to reinstall cabinets and the sink and we need a new/used set of cabinets to hold that double sink.

Theresa Perron

Town Administrator

## Page content

I will be back in the office Monday, September 16th, 2024.I will check my messages each day and will return your call as soon as I can.If you are making a tax or sewer payment please leave your payment in in the mail drip box in the door.Thank you for understanding and I apologize for any inconvenience.

Cindy

- Source URL: https://townofglover.com/town-hall-repairs/
- Final URL: https://townofglover.com/town-hall-repairs/

- Page type: post
- Published/updated: 2024-04-29T12:06:31+00:00 2024-04-29T12:06:31+00:00 2024-04-29T12:06:31+00:00 2026-07-13T21:06:00+00:00 2025-11-18T12:28:57+00:00 2023-01-27T14:04:58+00:00 2023-01-27T15:10:53+00:00 2026-07-13T21:09:14+00:00 2025-04-17T13:26:02+00:00 2025-04-29T11:55:56+00:00 2025-08-20T14:30:47+00:00

## Page content

Sending out a thank you to all who came out to help remove all furniture from the town hall this past Saturday morning.

Special thank you to those who leant us the trailers for three weeks in order to put them in storage.

The bathroom has been repaired including the floor and new plumbing. The ceilings in the main hall room have been repaired and painted, all the walls are painted, woodwork has been sanded, stained and polyed and today the sanding of all the wood flooring begins. Yet to do is the painting in the bathroom and new spot lights for the stage and of course the outside paintings and repairs.

Thanks to all who have been a guidance and a help.

Theresa

# Town of Glover has a new Website

- Source URL: https://townofglover.com/town-of-glover-has-a-new-website/
- Final URL: https://townofglover.com/town-of-glover-has-a-new-website/
- Crawled: 2026-07-30T19:10:57.326331+00:00
- Page type: post
- Published/updated: 2022-08-31T12:43:44+00:00 2022-08-31T13:34:45+00:00 2022-08-31T12:43:44+00:00 2022-08-31T13:34:45+00:00 2026-04-07T21:24:59+00:00 2026-01-28T20:35:52+00:00 2023-08-16T14:29:43+00:00 2024-02-22T13:26:00+00:00 2024-04-01T12:42:58+00:00 2024-09-25T16:19:30+00:00 2024-10-10T16:21:02+00:00 2026-07-13T21:05:17+00:00

## Page content

Come visit to stay informed about town business and happenings. The new site offers better access, less clicking, and more updated information. In particular, you can now view Recordings of Select Board Meetings and join Upcoming Zoom Meetings. You can also share all posts from the site as well as subscribe in the footer via email to all posts, as well as follow posts on Facebook.

# University of Vermont Survey – understanding mobility and housing needs from 2023 summer floods

- Source URL: https://townofglover.com/university-of-vermont-survey-understanding-mobility-and-housing-needs-from-2023-summer-floods/
- Final URL: https://townofglover.com/university-of-vermont-survey-understanding-mobility-and-housing-needs-from-2023-summer-floods/
- Crawled: 2026-07-30T19:11:00.016084+00:00
- Page type: post
- Published/updated: 2024-02-15T22:46:58+00:00 2024-02-15T22:46:58+00:00 2024-02-15T22:46:58+00:00 2022-07-11T19:14:13+00:00 2022-08-24T13:11:53+00:00 2026-02-16T14:07:17+00:00 2024-11-26T12:43:11+00:00 2024-11-26T14:44:15+00:00 2024-02-29T14:54:05+00:00 2024-02-29T14:54:49+00:00 2026-05-18T12:51:41+00:00 2026-05-26T14:35:52+00:00

## Page content

The University of Vermont is conducting a study to better understand mobility and housing needs of those affected by the 2023 summer floods. We are interested in hearing from people 18 and older whose housing, belongings or property were affected. The survey is available here:

go.uvm.edu/flood

Study participants will be entered into a raffle for a chance to win one of ten $50 gift cards to thank them for their time.

Thank you for your consideration.

Please contact the following people for more information:

Sarah Grajdura, PhDPostdoctoral AssociateDepartment of Civil and Environmental Engineering,The University of Vermontsarah.grajdura@uvm.edu

Dana Rowangould, PhDAssistant ProfessorDepartment of Civil and Environmental Engineering,The University of Vermontdana.rowangould@uvm.edu

## Page content

Please join us on Thursday, February 5, 2026, and Thursday, February 19, 2026, from 6:00pm – 8:00pm at the Glover Town Hall to discuss the 2026 Proposed Budget and Presentation in anticipation for Town Meeting. An agenda will be posted on the website, 3 physical locations, and Zoom will be available. Proposed budgets will be available, along with notes and clarifying explanations. Thank you!

## Page content

HURRY AND PLACE YOUR ORDER

February 14, 2025 – Glover Town Hall Valentine Sweetheart Dinner $25 by Alfreda’s Catering 5 p.m.Dam Dixieland Jazz Band – Starting at 6:30 p.m.Your Choice: Pork Tenderloin, Baked Stuffed Chicken BreastPotatoes, Maple Baked Winter Squash, Green BeansRoll, Dessert, Dine in Our Romantic Setting w/Music by Jim CurrierReservations only: Theresa@townofglover.com Include choice of meal, Name, Address, Number, Email.Reserved Town Hall Seatings 5 p.m. – 7 p.m. Takeout Pre-Ordered a Must.Delivery Tip AppreciatedQuestions, Reservations, or Volunteer Call: 802 525-7199 or 802 624-3463.All Proceeds for Shadow Lake Dam Fund. Donations Welcomed.Send Dinner Order & Check to Town of Glover, 51 Bean Hill Road, Glover, VT 05839 or dropyour check at the Town Clerk’s Office & memo: Attention: SLD Valentine Dinner.

## Page content

HELP NEEDED

We are creating a list of volunteers to help with the Recycling Center during the regular hours:

Wednesday, 12 a.m. to 3 p.m. and Saturdays 9 a.m. to 12 p.m.

We will rotate the list to avoid using the same persons twice in the same month.

Please call Theresa Perron to be put on that list at 802 525-6227.

# Wastewater Workshop- Stormwater & Lake Friendly Living!

- Source URL: https://townofglover.com/wastewater-workshop-stormwater-lake-friendly-living/
- Final URL: https://townofglover.com/wastewater-workshop-stormwater-lake-friendly-living/
- Crawled: 2026-07-30T19:11:06.051690+00:00
- Page type: post
- Published/updated: 2023-07-25T15:47:31+00:00 2023-07-25T15:47:31+00:00 2023-07-25T15:47:31+00:00 2026-05-27T15:34:12+00:00 2026-05-12T00:42:59+00:00 2026-06-25T22:00:32+00:00 2025-07-07T12:51:17+00:00 2026-03-09T11:17:25+00:00 2026-07-13T21:03:22+00:00

## Page content

Do you own lakefront property? Are you concerned about water quality in our lakes? Join us for a Wastewater Workshop on Saturday, July 29, 10am – 12:30pm at the West Glover Congregational Church (2516 Bean Hill Rd, West Glover). Led by Cristin Ashmankas, environmental analyst from the Vermont Department of Environmental Conservation, the workshop will share information on options for well-functioning, onsite wastewater systems and good maintenance practices for these systems on lakeshores. You will learn how you can save money and avoid costly emergency repairs while protecting our lakes and water quality with a properly managed system. Join us! The event is sponsored by the Orleans County Natural Resources Conservation District, the Town of Glover, Lake Parker Association and the Shadow Lake Association. Be Septic Smart!

# We hope to see you March 8, 2025 at the Box Supper Social Auction!

- Source URL: https://townofglover.com/we-hope-to-see-you-march-8-2025-at-the-box-supper-social-auction/
- Final URL: https://townofglover.com/we-hope-to-see-you-march-8-2025-at-the-box-supper-social-auction/
- Crawled: 2026-07-30T19:11:07.272347+00:00
- Page type: post
- Published/updated: 2025-03-03T17:22:22+00:00 2025-03-03T17:22:22+00:00 2025-03-03T17:22:22+00:00 2024-09-25T16:19:30+00:00 2024-10-10T16:21:02+00:00 2026-06-17T18:49:23+00:00 2026-07-13T21:06:00+00:00 2026-02-16T14:10:28+00:00 2024-05-16T13:11:41+00:00 2025-11-04T11:24:33+00:00 2025-11-04T19:16:48+00:00

## Page content

We have auctioneer Justin Lander to entertain us. Pack an embellished box, basket or pail with your specialty dinner foods for 2 and drink of your choice. Come join the fun! Your box will be auctioned off to the highest bidder. Everyone will gather at a Farmer’s Table to share their meal and conversation. This event will be at the Glover Town Hall, from 6 p.m. to 9 p.m. We plan to have music by Jeremy Harple and we invite you to bring an instrument to put together a “Kitchen Junket Band.”

All proceeds support the Shadow Lake Dam Fund.

RSVP or questions at 802 624-3463, 802 525-7199, theresa@townofglover.com, or 802 525-6227. http://shadowlakedam.org or http://townofglover.com – Send me an email I will be happy to send you the story of a box supper event I went to as a child.

Hope to see you there!
